question: What are the most influential papers on viral-vector gene therapy? Return 5 with DOIs and citation counts.
final_text: {"answer":"The most influential papers on viral-vector gene therapy, based on citation counts, include foundational work on lentiviral vectors for stable transduction, AAV-mediated liver transduction for hemophilia, and single-dose gene-replacement therapy for spinal muscular atrophy.","citations":[{"doi":"10.1126/science.272.5259.263","title":"In Vivo Gene Delivery and Stable Transduction of Nondividing Cells by a Lentiviral Vector","citation_count":4530},{"doi":"10.1038/nm1358","title":"Successful transduction of liver in hemophilia by AAV-Factor IX and limitations imposed by the host immune response","citation_count":1968},{"doi":"10.1056/nejmoa1706198","title":"Single-Dose Gene-Replacement Therapy for Spinal Muscular Atrophy","citation_count":1923},{"doi":"10.1128/jvi.72.3.2224-2232.1998","title":"Production of High-Titer Recombinant Adeno-Associated Virus Vectors in the Absence of Helper Adenovirus","citation_count":1255},{"doi":"10.1128/jvi.72.2.1438-1445.1998","title":"Membrane-Associated Heparan Sulfate Proteoglycan Is a Receptor for Adeno-Associated Virus Type 2 Virions","citation_count":1217}]}

parsed.answer: The most influential papers on viral-vector gene therapy, based on citation counts, include foundational work on lentiviral vectors for stable transduction, AAV-mediated liver transduction for hemophilia, and single-dose gene-replacement therapy for spinal muscular atrophy.
